categories.main_business_segments: Edison International is a holding company with two primary business segments: Southern California Edison Company (SCE), an investor-owned public utility engaged in supplying and delivering electricity to approximately 50,000 square miles of southern California, and Edison Energy, a global energy advisory firm providing integrated sustainability and energy solutions to commercial, industrial and institutional customers. SCE is the dominant operating entity and Edison Energy's activities are currently not material to report as a separate segment.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: SCE operates a diversified electricity generation portfolio including nuclear facilities (Palo Verde with 15.8% ownership and San Onofre undergoing decommissioning), hydroelectric generation, and renewable energy sources. The company utilizes transmission and distribution infrastructure to deliver electricity, and is investing in utility-owned energy storage projects (537.5 MW capacity), smart grid technologies, and advanced metering infrastructure. SCE also employs covered conductor programs and fast-curve protective settings to mitigate wildfire risk.
categories.primary_customers_markets: SCE serves approximately 50,000 square miles of southern California, providing electricity to residential, commercial, industrial and institutional customers. The company also serves customers through community choice aggregators (CCAs) and electric service providers. Edison Energy serves commercial, industrial and institutional customers globally seeking sustainability and energy solutions. SCE's customer base is subject to electrification trends driven by California's clean energy goals.
categories.geographic_coverage: Edison International operates primarily in southern California through SCE, which serves a 50,000 square mile service territory. SCE also owns and operates water and propane gas distribution systems on Catalina Island, California. Edison Energy operates globally, providing energy advisory services to commercial, industrial and institutional customers worldwide. The company has investments in emerging companies related to technology and business model changes in the energy sector.
categories.supply_chain_position: SCE operates as a vertically integrated utility positioned across the entire electricity supply chain: upstream (generation through owned and contracted power plants), midstream (transmission and distribution infrastructure), and downstream (retail delivery to end customers). The company procures electricity, capacity, environmental credits and ancillary services from its own generating plants and through contracts with energy producers. SCE also manages fuel supply contracts and engages in energy hedging activities.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Edison International's strategic priorities focus on leading the transformation of the electric power industry through: delivering clean energy, advancing electrification, building a modernized and reliable grid, and enabling customer technology choices. Key R&D and investment initiatives include grid modernization, renewable energy integration, energy storage deployment, electric vehicle charging infrastructure (Charge Ready programs), wildfire mitigation and prevention, climate adaptation investments, and support for California's decarbonization goals targeting net-zero GHG emissions by 2045.
categories.revenue_model: SCE generates revenue through regulated utility rates approved by the CPUC and FERC, comprising two main sources: earning activities (authorized operation and maintenance costs, depreciation, taxes and return on net investment in generation, transmission and distribution assets) and cost-recovery activities (CPUC and FERC-authorized balancing accounts for fuel costs, purchased power, public purpose programs, and specific operation and maintenance expenses). Edison Energy generates revenue through advisory services and energy solutions contracts with commercial and industrial clients.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: SCE faces competition from community choice aggregators (CCAs), electric service providers, and customer-owned distributed energy resources (solar, storage, efficiency). The FERC has opened transmission development to competition from independent developers. SCE is one of California's major investor-owned utilities alongside Pacific Gas & Electric Company (PG&E) and San Diego Gas & Electric Company (SDG&E). The company maintains investment-grade credit ratings (Baa1/Moody's, BBB/Fitch, BBB/S&P) and is positioned as a regulated utility with cost recovery mechanisms.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Edison International is a large-cap utility holding company with 2023 net income of $1.2 billion and core earnings of $1.8 billion. SCE's year-end rate base was $42.7 billion at December 31, 2023 (excluding AB 1054 excluded capital). The company forecasts $37.5 billion in total capital expenditures for 2024-2028, with weighted-average rate base expected to reach $60.6 billion by 2028. SCE's 2023 operating revenue was $16.3 billion. The company maintains a target dividend payout ratio of 45-55% of SCE's core earnings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Edison International differentiates through: industry-leading wildfire mitigation and safety programs, commitment to net-zero GHG emissions by 2045 aligned with California policy, significant investments in grid modernization and reliability ($1.0 billion in utility-owned storage, $13 billion in infrastructure replacement 2023-2028), comprehensive electrification support programs (Charge Ready), and integrated sustainability solutions through Edison Energy. The company emphasizes safe, reliable, resilient electricity delivery while enabling California's clean energy transition and supporting customer technology choices.
